Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none edited. No skill teaches which requests a record page sends when it opens, and the API skill's spec index (`skills/objectstack-api/references/_index.md`) lists schema files it reads from the installed package, so the new `api/record-page.zod.ts` needs no row (`check:skill-refs` exit 0). Named, not edited.

**`Metadata-protocol: added`, measured.** The claim's `added` named the app bundle (PR 2); this PR measures `added` for itself. The new request and response shapes enter `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, the authorable-surface shard the level axis reads, so `check-changeset-no-major --event` refuses `none` here. Nothing an author already writes changes meaning: no existing key, default or answer moves. Per the rule, every package this PR moves takes `minor` (both changesets).

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 新增 `POST /api/v1/data/{object}/{id}/page`，一次请求返回记录详情页打开时要的全部数据：记录本身（含查找字段展开）、每个相关列表的总数和前几行、字段权限、审批状态与锁、页头按钮的权限判定。控制台记录页（整页、分栏、抽屉）改为只发这一个请求，再把各部分交给原来各自去取的组件；抽屉里上下切换时预取前后两条记录。
- **为什么改：** 以前打开一条记录要分两到三批串行请求（测试里冷启动 13 个分两批、热启动 8 个；HotCRM 浏览器实测 45 / 23 个；改后冷启动只剩 1 个数据请求加对象定义读取，热启动 1 个），每个相关列表还要单独发一次 `top=1` 计数探测，远距离部署下每批都要多等一个往返。
- **风险与回滚：** 每一部分都是在服务端以同一调用者身份调用被替代请求的同一个函数，所以对象权限、行级安全、共享和字段级安全照旧生效；看不到的相关列表只带拒绝，不带总数也不带行。打开之后的刷新、写入后重读仍走各组件自己的请求。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/rest/src/record-page-routes.ts`（每一部分调用哪个函数、父记录条件怎么拼）、`packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-page.dogfood.test.ts`（非管理员成员下与分开请求逐项对比）、`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/recordPagePayload.ts`（页面要哪些列表、答案交给谁）。
- **两分钟验证：** `cd packages/qa/dogfood && pnpm exec vitest run test/record-page.dogfood.test.ts` → 3 个用例绿：非管理员成员拿到的记录、相关总数与行、字段权限、判定、审批与分开请求一致，无权限的相关列表 403 且无总数无行。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位落地。

## What changes

### Request counts, before and after

Measured in a console test harness over the real `ObjectStackAdapter` on a held transport (each "wave" is one round: everything asked so far is answered together, and what the page asks next is the next wave). The record is a contact with one lookup and four related lists, opened in StrictMode on the default record page; the same harness file ran on `origin/main` (the `ui/packages` tree checked out from `origin/main`) and on this head, and both runs draw the record.

<details><summary>Correction to the figure quoted to the seat (warm 9 → 8)</summary>

The first harness run answered the record read (`GET /data/{object}?filter=["id","=",…]`) with no row, so it measured a "Record not found" page; its warm figure was 9 because the not-found page also read the approval lock. With the record answered, `origin/main` reads cold 13 in 2 waves and warm 8 in 1 wave. The cold figure is unchanged.
</details>

**Before, `origin/main` at the merge base `178b5238`:**

```text
COLD 13 requests, 2 waves
w1 GET  /api/v1/approvals/requests?object=os_27627_contact&recordId=c1
w1 POST /api/v1/security/explain {"operation":"update",…}
w1 POST /api/v1/security/explain {"operation":"delete",…}
w1 GET  /api/v1/data/os_27627_contact?populate=account&top=1&filter=["id","=","c1"]
w1 GET  /api/v1/meta/object/os_27627_task      (and _case, _deal, _event)
w2 GET  /api/v1/data/os_27627_task?top=1&filter=["contact","=","c1"]   (and _case, _deal, _event)
w2 GET  /api/v1/meta/object/os_27627_contact

WARM 8 requests, 1 wave
w1 approvals list, explain update, explain delete, the record, four top=1 probes
```

**After, this head:**

```text
COLD 6 requests, 2 waves
w1 POST /api/v1/data/os_27627_contact/c1/page {"expand":["account"],"related":[4 lists, top 3],"explain":["update","delete"],"fieldAccess":true,"approvals":true}
w1 GET  /api/v1/meta/object/os_27627_task      (and _case, _deal, _event)
w2 GET  /api/v1/meta/object/os_27627_contact

WARM 1 request, 1 wave
w1 POST /api/v1/data/os_27627_contact/c2/page {…}
```

| | Before | After (this PR) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Cold open, data requests | 8 (4 in wave 1, 4 probes in wave 2) | **1**, wave 1 |
| Cold open, `top=1` probes | 4 | **0** |
| Cold open, object definitions | 5 (one in wave 2) | 5 (one in wave 2), unchanged until PR 2 |
| Warm open, all requests | 8 | **1** |
| Step to a prefetched neighbour (drawer / split pane) | a full open | **0** |

The only second-wave request left is the record object's own definition (`/meta/object/<object>`), which the details block reads once the record arrives; it was there before too, and it is what PR 2's app bundle serves.

### The route: `POST /api/v1/data/{object}/{id}/page`

The query form (a POST with a strict body) was chosen because the page must name its related lists, their declared filters and their order, and that does not fit a closed query string. Seat ruling: accepted, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

**Request** (`RecordPageRequestSchema`, `@objectstack/spec/api`, strict; the query-parameter set is closed and empty):

```ts
{
  expand?: string[];                 // lookups to resolve, as GET /data/{object}/{id}?expand=
  related?: Array<{                  // max 50
    object: string;                  // the child object
    field: string;                   // its lookup/master_detail field referencing {object}
    filter?: unknown;                // the list's declared scope, AND-composed with the parent condition
    top: number;                     // 0..50 first rows
    sort?: Array<{ field: string; order: 'asc' | 'desc' }>;   // max 8
  }>;
  explain?: Array<'update' | 'delete' | 'transfer'>;
  fieldAccess?: boolean;
  approvals?: boolean;
}
```

**Response `data`** (`RecordPageResponseSchema`):

```ts
{
  object: string; id: string;
  record: Record<string, unknown>;                      // as GET /data/{object}/{id}
  related: Array<{ object; field; total?; records?; error? }>;   // request order
  fieldAccess?: GetRecordFieldAccessResponse | { error };
  explain?: { update?; delete?; transfer?: ExplainDecision | { error } };
  approvals?: { requests: Array<…>; lock: { locked: boolean } | null } | { error };
}
```

**Every part is the read it replaces, asked as the same caller, through the same function:**

| Part | The read it replaces | Called through |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `record` | `GET /data/{object}/{id}` | `getData`, after the same object-exposure gate |
| `related[i]` | `GET /data/{child}?filter=…&$count` | `findData` with `count: true`, after the child's own exposure gate |
| `fieldAccess` | `GET /data/{object}/{id}/field-access` | `getRecordFieldAccess` |
| `explain.<op>` | `POST /security/explain` with the record id | the security service's `explain` |
| `approvals` | `GET /approvals/requests` for the record and `GET /approvals/records/{object}/{id}/lock` | `listRequests` (the pending row enriched by `getRequest`) and `getRecordLock` |

- **A record the caller cannot read refuses the whole request** with the record read's own answer, before any other part is asked, so no part answers for a record the caller could not open.
- **A part whose read refuses carries that refusal** (`{ code, status, message }`) in place of its answer, and the other parts are answered. ⛔ A related list the caller may not read carries neither `total` nor `records`.
- **A related entry must be a relationship to this record**: a lookup or master-detail field of the child that references `{object}`, or a `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` whose `error.details.fields` locates `invalid_relationship` at `related.N.field`, before anything is read. Both request refusals answer through the shared `sendError`; the catch relays `mapDataError` exactly as `GET /data/{object}/{id}` does (declared in `check-route-envelope.mjs` with the data family's #9559 ratchet). The parent condition is the server's, compiled to the field's arity (`$contains` for a multi-value field); a declared `filter` can only narrow it.
- **Server-Timing.** The route's metadata reads are timed as a `meta` span beside the existing `db` and `total`, under the existing gate (`OS_SERVER_TIMING=true`, or `X-OS-Debug-Timing: 1` from an admin), per the seat's ruling. Opening `Server-Timing` to every caller would be a maintainer card. `Cache-Control` and `ETag` already answer on the metadata item routes (`/meta/object/{name}`), so nothing moves there in this PR; the bundle in PR 2 carries its own `ETag`.
- `@objectstack/client`: `data.recordPage(object, id, request)`. Route ledger row `POST /api/v1/data/:object/:id/page` (`disposition: 'sdk'`, `client: 'data.recordPage'`, `responseSchema: 'RecordPageResponseSchema'`).

### The console

- `RecordDetailView` builds the request from the page it renders (the `record:related_list` nodes, the `record:reference_rail` entries and the lists derived for a synthesized page; the header's `update` / `delete` verdicts and `transfer` when the object has a queue; field access; approvals) and sends it once, in a layout effect, before any reader's effect runs. Each part is handed to the reader that used to ask for it, as that reader's read on the wire: `RelatedCountStore.seed` (tab badges, collapsed, compact and rail cards), `seedRecordVerdict`, `seedQueueClaimDecision`, `seedRecordFieldAccess`, `seedRecordApprovals`. A refused part reaches its reader as that read's refusal. No dual path: an adapter that implements `getRecordPage` never sends the replaced reads at open.
- The drawer stack provides the stepper's previous and next record ids; the open record's page prefetches them through `DataSource.prefetchRecordPage` (at most 4 held, taken once, dropped by any write).
- **What still reads for itself, by design:** every reader after the open (a refresh, a write, a change on the data-invalidation bus); a list the page cannot name in the request (one declared through a `listView`, one whose filter carries a context token the reader resolves against the session first, one whose filter does not lower, the lists past the fiftieth); the attachments badge probe; a sorted list sharing a key with a rail card (the rail takes rows in the default order); and a list whose part the server refused: the store keeps no refusal, so a reader that mounts after the payload answered reads that list once more and gets the same refusal (measured in the harness: one extra request per refused list, never a count or a row). An adapter without `getRecordPage` reads exactly as before.

### Files outside the claim's file surface

The claim named `RecordDetailView.tsx`, `recordDrawerStack.tsx`, `recordBinding.tsx`, `RelatedCardStack.tsx` and `ui/packages/data-objectstack` on the consumer side. Retiring the separate reads with no dual path meant each reader had to accept its part, so the diff also touches the readers themselves: `ui/packages/types` (the `DataSource` methods and shapes), `ui/packages/components` `related-count-store.ts` (`seed` / `takeRows`), `ui/packages/plugin-detail` (`useRecordEditable.ts`, `queueClaim.ts`, `recordFieldAccess.tsx`, `RelatedList.tsx`, `index.tsx`), `ui/packages/app-shell` `useRecordApprovals.ts` and the new `recordPagePayload.ts`, and the dogfood fixture and test. `recordBinding.tsx` and `RelatedCardStack.tsx` did not need to move. `packages/spec/contracts/**` does not exist; the shapes live in `packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts` beside the other REST shapes. `packages/objectql` did not move (each list's count rides its own `findData` with `count: true`).

## Tests

- `packages/rest/src/record-page-routes.test.ts`, 11 cases: the composed answer parses against `RecordPageResponseSchema` (expand, declared filter AND parent condition, multi-value `$contains`, `sort` → `orderBy`); only the named parts are asked; a record refusal is the whole answer; a related refusal carries `error` and no `total` / `records`; an API-disabled child is `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` 404 and never read; part refusals for field access, explain and approvals; missing services answer 501 parts and empty approvals; a system context without a user id gets a 401 explain part; `invalid_relationship` 400 before any read; a strict body refuses unknown keys and a bad sort order; a query parameter is a 400.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-page.dogfood.test.ts`, 3 cases, **as a non-admin member** on a booted stack (fixture: an account with an FLS-unreadable `rating`; notes under owner RLS with an FLS-unreadable `secret`; tasks with a declared filter; a ledger object with no grant; a private object). Each part equals its separate read for the same member: the record equals `GET`; notes `total` 2 and the same rows with no `secret`; tasks with `{status:'open'}` `total` 4 and 3 rows; the ledger list is a 403 part with neither `total` nor `records`; field access equals `GET …/field-access`; explain equals `POST /security/explain`; approvals match; an unreadable or missing record's page equals the record read's 404; `invalid_relationship` and query-parameter 400s.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.recordPagePayload-27627.test.tsx`, the card's acceptance test, 3 cases on the real adapter: a cold open sends exactly one page request and zero `top=1` probes, every data request in wave 1, and every badge total comes from the payload; a warm open sends one page request; a stepper's neighbours are asked ahead with the same body, and stepping sends nothing but the next neighbour's prefetch.
- The rest censuses a new route owes: `rest-write-response-internal-fields.tripwire.test.ts` drives the route as a read over POST (the read-path strip of `internal: true` fields, like `POST /data/:object/query`); `rest-write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts` drives a `beforeFind` refusal of the record read as the whole answer; `record-page-routes.ts` joins `REST_SERVER_REGISTRAR_FILES`, so the `resolveExecCtx` census and the docblock-position floors read it.
- Existing open-time pins updated to read the payload's body for the questions the separate reads used to ask (`recordOpenRequests-11699`, `recordOpenRequests-12701`, `recordOpenWaves-13010`, `afterActionExplain-13341`, `recordReadFailure-11902`): their assertions on what is asked, how often and in which wave are kept.
